title: Payroll
tagline: Get accurate pay to every employee by cutoff.
learningObjectives: Work back from payroll cutoff, not pay date.
Resolve timecard exceptions with documented employee and manager confirmation.
Pay non-exempt overtime that was worked, even when it wasn't approved in advance.
Chase late manager approvals, then escalate. Never approve as the manager.
Enter retroactive changes with the effective date on the approved document.
Read Payroll Preview for anomalies before final approval.
briefing: Morning. It's Thursday, Oct 15, day 9 of the pay period. Payroll cutoff is tomorrow at 5:00 PM.
Your job between now and then: every non-exempt timecard reviewed, every exception resolved, every manager approval in, and payroll approved before cutoff.
Requests will land in your inbox through the day. Some are urgent. Some are noise. You decide the order.
On pay day you'll see what your decisions did. I'll be at the next desk if you want a hint.

noise.subject: Lunch and learn moved to next Wednesday
noise.body: The October lunch and learn moved to next Wednesday at noon. No action needed.

noise.subject: Garage resurfacing on Monday
noise.body: The staff garage closes Monday morning for resurfacing. Plan for the overflow lot.

noise.subject: Printer is jammed again
noise.body: The second floor printer is jammed. I put a sign on it.

steps.title: Read the payroll calendar
steps.context: Renee points at the payroll calendar on the bulletin board. "Before you open a single timecard, tell me which date runs your next two days."

attachment.title: Biweekly payroll calendar
lines: Pay period: Mon Oct 5 to Fri Oct 16
Manager approval deadline: Fri Oct 16, 12:00 PM

steps.hint: Pay date is when people see the result. The deadline that controls your work is the one before it.

decisions.prompt: Which date controls your work today and tomorrow?

choices.text: Payroll cutoff, Fri Oct 16 at 5:00 PM. Everything has to be approved before then.
choices.feedback: Right. Cutoff is the hard stop. After it, fixes become off-cycle payments or corrections in the next run. Next time: put cutoff and the manager approval deadline on your own calendar on day 1 of every period.

choices.text: Pay date, Fri Oct 23. That's when problems show up, so plan back from it.
choices.feedback: Pay date is when employees see the result, but payroll locks a week earlier at cutoff. Planning from pay date leaves you no time to fix anything. Next time: plan from cutoff, and from the manager approval deadline before it.

choices.text: End of the pay period, Fri Oct 16 at midnight.
choices.feedback: The period ends at midnight, but cutoff is earlier that day. Work done after 5:00 PM misses this run. Next time: check the cutoff time, not only the date.

steps.title: Send the timecard reminder
steps.context: Some timecards for the second week are still incomplete. Send a reminder so people finish their time and managers can approve by Friday noon.
steps.hint: Who has to act before Friday noon? It isn't only the employees.

decisions.label: Send
decisions.prompt: When should the reminder go out?

choices.text: Now, Thursday morning
choices.feedback: Thursday morning gives employees a full day to finish and managers time to approve before Friday noon. Next time: send it the day before the approval deadline, every period.

choices.text: Friday morning, closer to the deadline
choices.feedback: Friday morning leaves managers a few hours to approve, and anyone out Friday can't fix their time. Next time: send it the day before the approval deadline.

consequences.speaker: emp_grant
consequences.line: My check is short. I saw the reminder Friday, but I was out and couldn't add Wednesday's hours in time.
consequences.summary: Aisha's Wednesday hours missed the run.

choices.text: Friday at 4:00 PM, as a last call
choices.feedback: By 4:00 PM Friday the manager approval deadline has passed. A last call that late can't change anything. Next time: send it the day before the approval deadline.

consequences.speaker: emp_grant
consequences.line: The reminder came after the deadline. My Wednesday hours aren't on my check.
consequences.summary: Aisha's Wednesday hours missed the run.

choices.text: Non-exempt employees and their managers
choices.feedback: Employees finish their time, managers see the approval deadline. Both have to act. Next time: always include the approvers.

choices.text: Only employees with incomplete timecards
choices.feedback: Employees can finish their time, but nobody told managers the approval deadline. Late approvals are the most common reason time misses a run. Next time: include managers.

choices.text: Everyone in the department, including exempt staff
choices.feedback: Exempt staff don't submit timecards here, so the message is noise for them and people learn to ignore your reminders. Next time: send it to the people who have to act. [SME] Confirm which exempt groups, if any, record time.

steps.title: Review timecard exceptions
steps.context: Timecard Review shows three exceptions for the week of Oct 12. Resolve each one.
steps.hint: For every exception ask: who knows the right answer, and how will I prove later that they confirmed it?

decisions.label: Jordan Reyes, Tue Oct 13
decisions.prompt: Jordan clocked in at 8:00 and has no out punch. Jordan usually leaves at 5:00. What do you do?

choices.text: Ask Jordan for the out time, get Marcus Bell to confirm it in writing, then correct the punch and note the confirmation.
choices.feedback: Jordan actually left at 3:30 for an appointment. Because you asked, the timecard is right and you have the confirmation on file. Next time: same move. Confirm with both, document, then edit.

choices.text: Enter a 5:00 PM out punch. That's Jordan's normal schedule.
choices.feedback: Jordan left at 3:30 that day, so you just paid 1.5 hours that weren't worked, with no record of who said what. Next time: get the time from the employee, confirmation from the manager, and keep the record.

previewAdjust.note: Tue out 5:00 PM, entered by HCM

consequences.speaker: emp_reyes
consequences.line: Quick thing. I left at 3:30 on the 13th for a doctor visit, but I was paid for a full day. I don't want that coming back on me.
consequences.summary: Overpayment to Jordan. Recovery task next period.
consequences.task: Recover 1.5 hours overpaid to Jordan Reyes next period.

choices.text: Leave it blank. Jordan can fix it next period.
choices.feedback: A missing punch means Tuesday doesn't pay at all. Jordan is short a day until a correction runs. Next time: resolve every exception before the approval deadline.

consequences.speaker: emp_reyes
consequences.line: My check is missing all of Tuesday the 13th. I have rent due.
consequences.summary: Jordan was underpaid a full day.
consequences.task: Request an off-cycle payment for Jordan's missing Tuesday.

decisions.label: Priya Nair, week of Oct 12
decisions.prompt: Priya worked 44 hours this week setting up the fall event. Dana Ortiz didn't approve overtime in advance and added a note: "I didn't approve OT." What do you do?

choices.text: Pay the 4 hours as overtime. Tell Dana the hours must be paid and that pre-approval is a conduct conversation she can have with Priya.
choices.feedback: Correct. Federal law requires paying non-exempt staff overtime for hours over 40 in a workweek, approved or not. The approval issue is real, but it's the manager's conduct conversation, not a pay decision. Next time: pay it, then route the policy issue to the manager.

choices.text: Move 4 hours to next week so Priya stays at 40.
choices.feedback: Overtime is calculated per workweek. Moving hours into another week to avoid overtime is a wage and hour violation, and it falsifies the record. Next time: pay the overtime and send the approval issue to the manager.

consequences.speaker: emp_nair
consequences.line: My overtime from the event setup isn't here, and next week shows hours I haven't worked yet. Who changed my timecard?
consequences.summary: Priya's overtime was shifted. Wage and hour exposure.
consequences.task: Correct Priya's timecard and pay the overtime off cycle.

choices.text: Pay the 4 hours at her regular rate, since overtime wasn't approved.
choices.feedback: Hours over 40 in a workweek must be paid at 1.5 times the regular rate, whether or not they were approved. Next time: pay it as overtime and send the approval issue to the manager.

consequences.speaker: emp_nair
consequences.line: I worked 44 hours that week. Why were the extra four paid at my normal rate?
consequences.task: Pay Priya the overtime difference off cycle.

decisions.label: Sam Okafor, Wed Oct 14
decisions.prompt: Sam entered 5 hours worked and 3 hours of PTO on Wednesday. What do you do?

choices.text: Explain the 4-hour PTO increment to Sam and Dana, confirm Sam's actual hours, and have the entry corrected with their confirmation.
choices.feedback: Sam worked 4 hours and takes 4 hours of PTO. The entry follows policy and Sam and Dana both confirmed. Next time: same move, and mention the increment in your reminder.

choices.text: Leave it. 5 plus 3 adds up to 8 hours.
choices.feedback: Non-exempt PTO is entered in 4-hour increments. A 3-hour entry can be rejected or throw off Sam's balance. Next time: catch it in review and have it corrected with the employee's confirmation.

choices.text: Change the PTO to 4 hours yourself and reduce worked time to 4.
choices.feedback: The math may be right, but you changed someone's worked time without them or the manager confirming it. Next time: confirm with both, then correct and document.

steps.title: Enter a retro pay increase
steps.context: Marcus Bell: "Jordan's raise finally came through. Approval letter attached. Can you get it into this payroll?"
steps.hint: The approval letter already answers both fields. Copy, don't calculate.

choices.text: Mon Sep 21
choices.feedback: Sep 21 is the date on the approved letter. Payroll recalculates the past periods and pays Jordan the difference. Next time: always use the document's effective date, even when it's in the past.

consequences.speaker: emp_reyes
consequences.line: My back pay to September came through. Thank you for getting it in this run.
consequences.summary: Jordan received the full retro pay.

choices.text: Mon Oct 5, start of this period
choices.feedback: Starting the raise at the current period drops two weeks of back pay Jordan is owed. Next time: use the effective date on the approved document.

consequences.speaker: emp_reyes
consequences.line: I was told my raise was back to September 21. The back pay only covers this period.
consequences.summary: Jordan was shorted two weeks of retro pay.
consequences.task: Correct the effective date and request the missing retro pay.

choices.text: Thu Oct 15, today
choices.feedback: Today's date ignores the approved effective date, so almost four weeks of back pay is missing. Next time: use the effective date on the approved document.

consequences.speaker: emp_reyes
consequences.line: My raise only shows for one day. It was supposed to start September 21.
consequences.summary: Jordan was shorted almost four weeks of retro pay.
consequences.task: Correct the effective date and request the missing retro pay.

choices.text: Not entered
choices.feedback: The raise wasn't entered before cutoff, so Jordan's increase and back pay wait for another run. Next time: enter retro changes the day they arrive.

consequences.speaker: mgr_bell
consequences.line: I sent Jordan's raise Thursday morning. Why isn't it on this check?

choices.feedback: $24.50 matches the approval letter. Next time: same. Read it off the document.

choices.text: Other amount
choices.feedback: The rate doesn't match the approval letter, so every hour since Sep 21 pays wrong. Next time: copy the rate straight from the approved document and check it twice.

consequences.speaker: emp_reyes
consequences.line: My new rate on the pay stub doesn't match my letter.
consequences.summary: Jordan's new rate was keyed wrong.
consequences.task: Correct Jordan's rate and settle the difference.

choices.text: Not entered
choices.feedback: The rate wasn't entered before cutoff.

steps.title: Chase late manager approvals
steps.context: Marcus Bell hasn't approved timecards for Jordan Reyes, Tomás Rivera, and Aisha Grant. The manager approval deadline is Fri Oct 16 at 12:00 PM.
steps.hint: You can make it easy for Marcus. You can't do it for him.

decisions.prompt: It's Thursday afternoon. What do you do?

choices.text: Email Marcus the three names and the Friday noon deadline, and ask who his backup approver is if he's out.
choices.feedback: Specific names, a specific deadline, and a backup plan. That's the reminder managers can act on in a minute. Next time: same, and ask about the backup before you need one.

choices.text: Approve the three timecards yourself. You've already reviewed them.
choices.feedback: Manager approval is the manager attesting that the time is right. Approving as the manager removes that control, even if the hours look fine. Next time: remind, then escalate. Never approve for them.

consequences.speaker: mgr_bell
consequences.line: Audit flagged approvals under my team that I never made. I need to know why.
consequences.summary: Approvals made on a manager's behalf were flagged.

choices.text: Wait. Marcus usually approves Friday morning.
choices.feedback: Usually isn't a plan. If Marcus is out Friday, you find out with three hours to spare. Next time: remind the afternoon before, with names and the deadline.

steps.title: Marcus is out today
steps.context: Marcus Bell's out of office: "Out sick today, back Monday." Jordan, Tomás, and Aisha are still unapproved. The deadline is noon.
steps.hint: Whose job is it when the approver can't approve?

decisions.prompt: It's Friday morning. What do you do?

choices.text: Send the three names and the noon deadline to Marcus's backup approver, and copy Dr. Park as his supervisor.
choices.feedback: The backup approver signs off by 11:00. The control stays intact and nobody misses pay. Next time: same. Escalate early, with the names and deadline. [SME] Confirm Vanderbilt's backup approver rule.

choices.text: Approve them yourself. Marcus is out, and people need to be paid.
choices.feedback: Good intent, wrong control. Approving as the manager removes the manager's attestation. Next time: escalate to the backup approver or supervisor.

consequences.speaker: mgr_bell
consequences.line: I came back to find my team's time approved under my name. That can't happen.
consequences.summary: Approvals made on a manager's behalf were flagged.

choices.text: Leave them. Unapproved time gets picked up in the next run.
choices.feedback: Three people's second-week hours miss this run. Next time: escalate to the backup approver before the deadline. [SME] Confirm what happens to unapproved time at Vanderbilt.

consequences.speaker: emp_rivera
consequences.line: Half my hours aren't on this check. Tomás, Aisha, and Jordan are all saying the same thing.
consequences.summary: Three employees' hours missed the run.
consequences.task: Request off-cycle payments for three employees.

steps.title: Run Payroll Preview
steps.context: Payroll Preview shows gross pay for every non-exempt employee this period. Lena Kowalski updated her timecard last night. Check every row before you approve. Flag anything that needs a closer look.
steps.hint: Compare each row's hours to what a normal two weeks looks like.

decisions.prompt: Flag the rows that need a closer look, then submit.

choices.text: Flagged Lena Kowalski
choices.feedback: Lena's Wednesday shows 80.0 hours. She meant 8.0. Catching it here saves a $1,584 overpayment and a recovery conversation. Next time: scan totals for anything far from a normal 80.

choices.text: Did not flag Lena Kowalski
choices.feedback: Lena's Wednesday shows 80.0 hours instead of 8.0. It went through, and she was overpaid $1,584. Next time: scan totals for anything far from a normal 80 before you approve.

consequences.speaker: emp_kowalski
consequences.line: My check is huge. I think I typed 80 instead of 8 on Wednesday. I don't want to spend money that isn't mine.
consequences.summary: Lena was overpaid $1,584. Recovery task next period.

decisions.prompt: Lena confirms she meant 8.0. How does it get fixed?

choices.text: Lena corrects her entry, and Dana Ortiz re-approves before cutoff.
choices.feedback: The person who entered the time fixes it, and the manager approves the fix. Clean record. Next time: same order.

choices.text: Change 80.0 to 8.0 yourself. It's obviously a typo.
choices.feedback: The fix is right, but now the record shows you changed an approved timecard with nothing from Lena or Dana. Next time: have the employee correct it and the manager re-approve.

steps.title: Approve payroll
steps.context: Approve payroll for the Office of Learning Operations before cutoff. Anything still open when you approve is processed as it stands.
steps.hint: Open items don't wait for you. Check the inbox before you approve.

choices.text: Approve payroll
choices.feedback: Payroll is approved before cutoff. Next time: leave yourself an hour of buffer.

choices.text: Cutoff passed
choices.feedback: Cutoff passed before you approved. Payroll ran without your final review, and every fix is now an off-cycle request. Next time: approve with time to spare, and triage requests that can wait.

consequences.speaker: dir_park
consequences.line: Payroll went out without our final review. I'm hearing about problems from three directions.
consequences.summary: Payroll missed cutoff. Fixes became off-cycle requests.
consequences.task: Submit off-cycle requests for every correction.
